justifications.durability: the test drives the production path rather than a hand-built event: tests/test_ticker_shows_the_lane_mean.py:185 builds each row through recovery._watch_transition over a temp host layer's declared lane document, so the shape under assertion is the shape a live row carries -- the prior review's durability dock was precisely that no test reached the producer. The pair is asserted against the run's own rate and the lane mean as two distinct constants (test file :194), three parametrised means prove the figure follows the document rather than a constant, and the absent/stale/non-JSON/no-mean cases each assert the named phrase, so the guard fails on the regressions it names. The negative control reddens the lane-figure assertions when the mean is dropped. Docked one because the config resolution and the reuse window have no case of their own, so a regression in the four-layer lookup would not be caught by the suite.
justifications.evidence: the reviewed run's own two-arm gate and negative control were read from disk, not from the manifest. gate/baseline_suite_final.log ran at base 7fbe5fd89 and reads '13 failed, 394 passed' EXIT=1; gate/after_suite_final.log reads '3 failed, 404 passed' EXIT=1; the head arms' three failing ids (test_cli_follow_streams_each_event_as_one_json_document, test_cli_follow_prints_compact_transition_lines_by_default, test_cli_follow_keeps_machine_objects_behind_json_flag) are all present in the base arm's thirteen, so the added failure set is empty and derived 0. gate/negative-control-repair.log shows EXIT=1 with 4 failures on the declared mutation, all four assertions that read the lane figure, none of them an id the head arm fails. I re-ran the focused file at head (12 passed) as an independent positive control. Docked three: the head arm's own header line records revision=c9d65a030, the commit before the repair 6c73fea3b that the tree actually carried, so the code identity rests on the manifest's revision_note rather than on the log; and the manifest cites gate/ruff-head-repair.log and gate/ruff-head-format-repair.log, whose snapshots show a W292 and a second format finding the final head no longer has (I measured the head files: ruff check clean, ruff format reports only the pre-existing ticker.py STATS hunk the base reports too), so a reader reconciling the cited logs against the manifest's 'ruff clean' claim meets an inconsistency the final tree does not.
justifications.fit: lane_rate_text, lane_document_path, lane_mean_from_text, _lane_mean and _lane_cells at reckon/crew/ticker.py:729-1490 follow the module's existing cell idiom (bound_cells at :716, _spend_cells at :1724, _stats at :1753): each returns a list of (text, style) tuples and the renderer appends them. The new constants are named by what they measure (LANE_LABEL, LANE_MEAN_UNAVAILABLE, LANE_DOCUMENT_REUSE_SECONDS), the import of lane_document reuses the reader every other consumer carries, and no name carries a version, a plan label or a tracker reference.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node's section measure is that the ticker never shows a run's own generation rate without the lane's mean beside it; reckon/crew/ticker.py:1458 _lane_cells composes ' 2.00 lane 1.44' from the run's rate and the lane's mean, and at :1631 the row appends it. The prior landing read the mean from event['lane_reading'], a key no producer sets; the repair takes it from the lane document the row's own backend declares (ticker.py:768 lane_document_path resolves flight.resolve(project).config -> backends[backend].lane_document, :801 lane_mean_from_text parses it through reckon/crew/lane_document.py's readers, :1425 _lane_mean caches it for LANE_DOCUMENT_REUSE_SECONDS=15.0). The fields the cell reads off the event -- project, backend (recovery.py:9838-9849) and spend_generation_rate (recovery.py:9953) -- are all set by the production builder _watch_transition (recovery.py:9810), and the host flight config declares lane_document for the local lane (flight.yaml:352, backend clive). The cell is therefore reachable end to end, which is exactly what the previous review (total 92) found it was not; docked one because a row naming no backend adds no cell and a pane at its minimum grid width drops it (ticker.py:1631), both disclosed in the fragment, so at those edges neither figure shows.
justifications.scope_discipline: the cumulative diff against base touches exactly three paths -- reckon/crew/ticker.py, tests/test_ticker_shows_the_lane_mean.py and docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/ticker-shows-the-lane-mean.html -- all inside the manifest's declared write paths; no other file is changed and no shared state, plan or index is touched. The two behaviours the measure did not imply (no cell for a row naming no backend, and the cell dropped at the grid's minimum width) are stated in the fragment and in the code docstrings rather than smuggled.
